gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the LiTime 48V 30A charger it recommended for fast charging puts out at least 1,536 W (51.2 V × 30 A) for about 3.5 hours on a 48V 105Ah cart pack. That is more than the 1,440 W continuous limit of a standard 15 A, 120 V garage circuit (15 A × 120 V × 80%) before any conversion loss is added. The Lester Summit II 650W draws under 8 A from the wall, but at lithium voltages it delivers only about 11–13.5 A.
standout_why: Pages compared: iwantgolf.com (cited), Canyon Lake Mobile (rank 1), mydrivecar.com (rank 4) and mygolftutor.com (rank 7). iwantgolf works out cost per amp for Battery Tender, FORM and HTAXSCC, but none of ChatGPT's picks, and it says outright that no wall input figures are given. Canyon Lake lists the Lester 650W at '~13–17A @ 48V' with no input draw and a $650–$850 price range. mydrivecar says the LiTime 30A peaks at about 1,750 W and needs 3.3 h for 100Ah, but never compares that with what a household outlet can carry. mygolftutor gives output volts and amps only. The Trojan compatibility PDF (cited) would not render as text, so I could not check it.
decides: It changes ChatGPT's 'best fast charging' pick. The LiTime 30A is only fast if the shopper has a dedicated 20 A circuit, because on a shared 15 A garage circuit its constant-current stage runs longer than the NEC's 3-hour continuous-load threshold. On a 15 A outlet, the 18A LiTime ($155.99, about 5.8 h for 105Ah, 1,051 W maximum output) is the practical value pick. The Vatrer 20A lists a maximum AC input of 13 A, which also sits above 12 A, though the listing does not say at what voltage. The Lester's real advantage is a sub-8 A wall draw and IP66, but it costs about $30/A against $7–$11/A for the others. Owners of the Vatrer 105Ah or Redodo 48V 100Ah kits already get an 18 A 58.4 V charger in the box.
